criteria.text: Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the edits it actually made and the feedback it received (no post-hoc rationalization, no lucky guess)?
Did each refinement stage (lint, test) do real, feedback-responsive work toward the solution rather than cosmetic or no-op changes?

The atomic pointer wrapper constructs from an owned boxed node by leaking the node to a raw pointer, wrapping that in a heap-allocated atomic cell, and storing the pointer to that atomic cell — establishing two distinct levels of indirection (a stable atomic cell plus the swappable node behind it).
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #1 (BoxedAtomicPtr) / Known pitfalls: Double indirection

criteria.text: The node-view helper atomically loads the current node pointer with acquire-strength ordering and returns None when the load is null rather than dereferencing it.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #1 (node_view) / Known pitfalls: Null handling

criteria.text: Dropping a deferred boxed-atomic-pointer reclaims the heap-allocated atomic cell itself (reconstructing its owning Box and dropping it), guarding against null, while dropping a deferred node frees the node — the two drop paths free the correct, distinct allocations.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #2 (Deferred + Drop) / Known pitfalls: Double indirection

criteria.text: On a successful compare-exchange install, the replaced old node is handed to epoch-based deferred reclamation (not freed immediately), so concurrent readers cannot observe a freed node.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #3 (NodeView cas success) / Known pitfalls: Immediate vs. deferred free

criteria.text: On a failed compare-exchange, the replacement box that was leaked before the exchange is promptly reclaimed (freed directly, since it was never published), preventing a leak.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #3 (NodeView cas failure) / Known pitfalls: Leaking the replacement on failed CAS

criteria.text: A failed compare-exchange returns Err(None) when the slot was concurrently emptied (null load) and Err(Some(view)) reflecting the actual current node otherwise.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #3 (NodeView cas failure) / Known pitfalls: Null handling

criteria.text: The code asserts the invariant that a node's high-bound and next-sibling fields are simultaneously both set or both unset.
criteria.contract_ref: Solution decomposition #3 / Known pitfalls: Invariant assertion

criteria.text: In the non-fault build, debug_delay resolves to a compile-time-constant false, while the fault-injection build sometimes returns true; the fault path is not hard-coded off.

The implementation genuinely uses epoch-based reclamation and RCU node machinery for the tree rather than delegating to an off-the-shelf map (Mutex<BTreeMap>, RwLock, DashMap, etc.) behind the same API.
